A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Dysprosium (디스프로슘) itself — the sovereign of the Dysprosium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: late twenties — a graceful grown-up face with soft, smooth contours; no wrinkles, folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: a glamorous, sultry allure; bronze-brown skin; delicate V-line face with a small, soft chin; medium-sized eyes — feline cat eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; gracefully arched brows; straight narrow nose; soft, full lips; pale gold eyes that shimmer like heat haze over sand; smoky dark eye makeup.
Body and hair: hourglass-figured — full bust and hips, distinctly narrow-waisted build; glossy spiral drill curls with side-swept bangs; bright silver hair rippling with a heat-haze shimmer and faint pale-lime glints.
Expression: a cool, knowing look.
Her element, carried in her design: dysprosium: a bright silvery metal named in 1886 from the Greek for 'hard to get at', after more than thirty patient precipitations were needed to pull it out of holmium oxide, and only isolated as a pure metal decades later; a small share of it inside neodymium magnets keeps their pull when the motors of electric cars and wind turbines run hot; with iron and terbium it makes a metal that sings in a magnetic field, and its lamps give the white light of film and stage.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY
Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: dragon-scale armor covering the body with horn-shaped shoulder and head ornaments — a beastly, imposing silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: bright silver, heat-haze gold, pale lime yellow, motor-heat orange.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: a mirage kingdom in a sea of dunes: a citadel of silver dragon-scale towers that always shimmers one dune farther away in the heat haze, a lodestone gate that stays sealed even in the furnace heat of noon, a hidden oasis few travellers ever find.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Dy) and atomic number (66) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
